intro: Every plant in the botanic garden's glasshouse bloomed on the same night. The labels in the pots had all been rewritten, each in the same careful copperplate, and by morning the gardeners found the old catalogue pages stacked in the potting shed like kindling, every entry crossed out and begun again under the glass roof's first light. The head gardener says nothing about it, but she has set the register by the door to face the dawn, and this evening she was seen wiping the brass hooks where each page rests, one after another, as though expecting a signature.
echo: Pull it from the soil and its scream, they say, will kill you.

puzzles.title: Bolting
puzzles.flavor: The spy always carried a novel. This page will have to do.

blocks.text: Every plant in the botanic garden's glasshouse bloomed on the same night. The labels in the pots had all been rewritten.

hints: The first number in each pair never goes past the number of words on the page. What does the second count?

puzzles.title: Latin Names
hints: Each word stands for a letter, the way radio operators spell. Do those letters read? If not, try the alphabet backwards.

puzzles.title: Night Bloom
puzzles.flavor: Some squares have been given to you for free.
hints: The numbers describe runs of filled squares. What picture could they be drawing?

puzzles.title: Grafting
puzzles.flavor: Every one stopped at a different moment, and none can agree which hand is which.
hints: Imagine each of these as a person holding two flags out at arm's length. Sailors had an alphabet for that.

puzzles.title: Hardening Off
puzzles.flavor: The clerk ran out of alphabet and kept going anyway.
hints: Which short words are most common in English? Could any of them be hiding here?

meta.title: Meta: The Glasshouse
meta.flavor: The last lock takes every signature at once.
hints: Blaise de Vigenère needed a key to open this. Has every answer signed its work?
